subject: Unlocking the Software Factory: Agents, Loops, and Automated Language Improvement
body:
Hello First Name,

This week's 🦄 ai that works session was on "Unlocking the Software Factory: Agents, Loops, and Automated Language Improvement"!

The full recording, code, and diagrams from the session are now available on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We covered a lot on building a software factory for agent tools and driving automatic improvements to our programming language through persistent feedback loops. Here's a super quick recap:

*   **More Than Just One Prompt: It's a Multi-Stage Agent System:** We learned that a software factory isn't just one big prompt. It uses a team of specialized agents for different jobs: coding, analyzing chat logs, deduplicating issues, drafting PRs, responding to reviews, and even pruning stale issues. This multi-stage approach creates a continuous feedback loop, constantly improving our language.
*   **Humans Keep Things on Track and High Quality:** People are essential for auditing agent-generated issues, refining problem definitions, guiding suggested fixes, and reviewing/merging agent-generated PRs. This ensures everything stays high-quality and strategically aligned.
*   **Data Fuels Language Development:** The rich data from agent runs is incredibly valuable. Things like chat logs, issues, PRs, costs, and even the number of turns an agent takes, all inform our language design. This data helps us write better compiler error messages and refine the documentation or prompts that define an agent's capabilities. It's how we achieve continuous improvement.

If there's one key takeaway from this session:
You don't have to build an entire software factory all at once. Start small! Find a few isolated problems where agents can add value, then gradually connect those small loops. Focus on finding the best ways for humans and agents to work together, integrating them step-by-step, and slowly automate more of your development process.

If you have any questions, reply to this email or ask on Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We read every message! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
